name: Matterhorn Peak and Whorl Mountain
region: Sierra Nevada, northern Yosemite (Horse Creek Pass)

legs.connect: Walk back down to the tarn camp past the pass, then on another morning contour around the base of Whorl to the gullies that lead into its upper cliffs.

how: Both summits are reached from a camp just over Horse Creek Pass, so parties hike in on one day, climb Matterhorn that afternoon or the next, and take Whorl the following morning. Matterhorn is mostly class 2 talus with a move or two of easy third class near the top. Whorl is the more involved of the two: a series of chutes and ledges, a squeeze past a chockstone, and a ledge across the west face, with only short stretches of class 3.
descent: Return to the camp from each summit by the same ground, then follow the steep use trail down the talus slope to the trailhead on the way out.
logistics: Start from the Twin Lakes backpacker parking; the camp is near the headwaters of Spiller Creek just past the pass. Wilderness permit needed; summer to early fall is the usual window.
notes: Neither report names the route used on either peak, so route is null. Both parties climbed the peaks on separate days from the same camp; no traverse between them. The second report also did Twin Peaks and Virginia Peak from the same camp (Twin-Virginia ridge has loose class 3). Both reports are single trips by small parties, so confidence is medium.

name: Sawtooth Peak and Needham Mountain
region: Sierra Nevada, Mineral King (Sequoia National Park)

legs.route: Traverse from Sawtooth Peak (class 2-3), finishing on class 3 summit rocks
legs.connect: Follow the ridge south, dropping to roughly 11,500 feet to get around the towers, then climb the sandy slope to the summit.

how: Climbers go up the trail past the Monarch Lakes to Sawtooth Pass, scramble the class 2 ridge to Sawtooth, then continue along the crest toward Needham. The traverse is class 2-3 and avoids the ridge towers by dropping below them. Needham's summit area has a couple of steep class 3 pinnacles, so the top takes some care. The same two peaks are also done in the opposite order from a camp near Franklin Pass, approaching Needham cross-country first.
descent: Head down Needham's sandy southwest slope to Amphitheater Lake, then cross Crystal Pass keeping to easier ground and follow the trail down by Crystal Lake to the trailhead.
logistics: Mineral King trailhead; budget roughly 11 to 12 hours for the loop. Cars should be protected from marmots in early season. Summer through early fall is the usual window.
notes: The 2002 party did Needham first (class 2 southwest side) then Sawtooth southwest face, from Franklin Pass camp via Soda Creek; the 2025 party did Sawtooth first then traversed. The 2025 report gives the higher class (2-3) for the ridge. A further log not fetched calls the traverse class 3.
